fdx_field_map.source: plaid/core-exchange, branch mj-add-corex-6.4, versions/6.4/corex.yaml (info.version: 6.4.0), commit 5b1c4c6daf7bb4bdb84d13e67917023278b8366c, fetched via `gh api repos/plaid/core-exchange/contents/versions/6.4/corex.yaml?ref=mj-add-corex-6.4` -- the AccountDescriptor, DepositAccountDescriptor, DepositAccount, Transaction, and DepositTransaction schema objects, plus the shared Currency type they reference. Superseded a first draft built from Plaid's browsable 6.3 reference docs; the 6.3 draft had invented three fields the real 6.4 schema does not have on these objects -- see the three removed rows below and spec/fdx-6.4-mapping.md.
fdx_field_map.account.accountId: resources.list observation.provider_id, and status.read/balances.read/history.read observation.resource_id is a Sumer-assigned local mapping (fdx-checking-1) of it
fdx_field_map.account.accountType: provider_extra.fdx_accountType on the resources.list observation (Sumer's resource 'kind' is a coarse-grained mapping: bank_checking)
fdx_field_map.account.accountNumberDisplay: provider_extra.fdx_accountNumberDisplay on the resources.list observation (already a display-masked placeholder in FDX itself)
fdx_field_map.account.currency.currencyCode: the 'asset' field of both balance AmountWires (USD)
fdx_field_map.transactions[].transactionId: history observation.provider_id, and the tail of local_id
fdx_field_map.transactions[].amount: provider_extra.fdx_amount_unsigned (the untouched FDX absolute value, as a decimal string) AND the signed history observation.amount (see debitCreditMemo mapping below) -- both are kept so no information is lost by the DEBIT/CREDIT-to-sign normalization
fdx_field_map.transactions[].debitCreditMemo: provider_extra.fdx_debitCreditMemo (verbatim) AND the sign of observation.amount (DEBIT -> negative, CREDIT -> positive; observation.raw_sign is fixed at provider_negative for this adapter, meaning: once normalized, a negative amount means a debit)
fdx_field_map.transactions[].status: provider_extra.fdx_status (verbatim, one of PENDING/POSTED/AUTHORIZATION/MEMO) AND observation.posting (PENDING->pending, POSTED->posted, AUTHORIZATION and MEMO->unknown, since Sumer's posting enum only has three states -- txn-0003 exercises the AUTHORIZATION->unknown leg so the LOSSY column has no silent case)
fdx_field_map.transactions[].transactionTimestamp: provenance.observed_at when postedTimestamp is absent (txn-0001, txn-0003); provider_extra.fdx_transactionTimestamp always
fdx_field_map._removed_from_6.3_draft: account.balanceAsOf, transactions[].accountId, and transactions[].currency all appeared in an earlier draft of this payload sourced from Plaid's browsable 6.3 docs. None exist on 6.4's DepositAccount/Transaction schema objects: balanceAsOf is real in 6.4 but only on InvestmentAccount (not DepositAccount); Transaction carries no accountId at all (the account is scoped by the request path, /accounts/{accountId}/transactions, not repeated per-transaction); Transaction carries no currency field (only foreignCurrency, paired with foreignAmount, for the foreign-amount case this fixture does not exercise). All three were removed from the payload rather than kept as 6.3-only fields, per Ruling A6: 6.4 wins.
fdx_field_map.balances.read observation.provenance.obs: NOT an FDX-sourced mapping: 6.4's DepositAccount has no per-balance timestamp field (unlike InvestmentAccount's balanceAsOf). Provenance.observed_at is adapter-claimed evidence (spec/observation.md section 1), so this adapter stamps its own fetch-time clock reading here -- there is no source field to lose, so this is not a Lossy entry.

expect.notes: Every FDX field named in fdx_field_map lands somewhere named there -- either as a first-class Sumer field or, for anything without a Sumer equivalent (account type/category/nickname/masked number, the untouched unsigned amount, the raw debitCreditMemo and status strings), verbatim in provider_extra with an fdx_-prefixed key so it is visibly provenance rather than a Sumer concept. That claim is now MACHINE-CHECKED in both directions: the runner scans every provider_extra.<key> the map names and requires it to have arrived on the wire (nothing is silently dropped), and requires every provider_extra key that DID arrive to be named by the map (nothing arrives undocumented). The direction that catches an undocumented key reads every provider_extra the adapter emitted ANYWHERE -- the resources.list descriptor and every observation in expect.ledger's sequences, not only the records that survived folding -- so a key smuggled in on a row that is later superseded or tombstoned is still a key that arrived undocumented. expect.ledger additionally pins each provider_extra's full contents EXACTLY -- key sets and values both -- so a dropped or mangled value fails as loudly as a dropped key, and pins the three transactions' ORDER, which a live-set membership list could not: the AUTHORIZATION row arriving before the POSTED one is a different history, and the same three keys. spec/fdx-6.4-mapping.md's LOSSY column, gated by this fixture, is therefore empty for every row this fixture covers because the suite says so, not because the prose does. The prose in each fdx_field_map value stays documentation: the runner reads the provider_extra.<key> targets out of it and nothing else.
